sessions.note: Round 16 entered from the RA-solver Phase-2 vectors. STRUCTURAL RESULT: candidate_stream51.c (memory/wip/func_8007C7A0/) is the first body whose 51 instructions match target one-for-one in opcode, operand shape and order - no missing/extra/reordered insn. Verified identically on the twin func_8007C86C (both 51/51 insns, sandbox --disable all score 15). Score 15 > the documented 12 ONLY because masked-Levenshtein counts renames; frame51's 13 included two WRONG insns, this has none. Two levers, both from reading target's asm rather than searching: (1) s16 carrier instead of s32 - target insn 1 `move a3,a0` copies the RAW halfword before sign-extension and the join copy `move a3,v0` carries no extension, so an s32 carrier forces sll/sra at the join and drops the entry move (that was frame51's 2-insn error); (2) a named tail temp `pkt = lo | 0xE3000000; return hi | pkt;` - written as `return hi | (lo|C)` GCC reassociates to `(hi|C)|lo` while target computes `(lo|C)|hi`. MECHANISM (ra_solver model reproduces our dispositions 11/11; tmp/c7a0_what_if.py finds an EXACT 9/9 target allocation from three deltas): (a) `hi` must conflict with both limit-saves and both sign-extends, i.e. be live from before the x-clamp; (b) tx and lo must lose their $a0 preference; (c) lo must lose its $v0 hard conflict. Root causes read from tools/gcc-2.7.2 source: the $a0 preference originates at `76 = a0` (carrier init) and PROPAGATES to tx and lo via global.c:851's REG_DEAD-linked copy merge, stopping only if the allocnos conflict; find_reg takes the LOWEST preferred reg so $a0 beats a free $v0. MIPS has NO REG_ALLOC_ORDER in this tree, so both local-alloc and global-alloc scan ascending - $a2/$a3 are reachable ONLY by exclusion (hard conflict or regs_someone_prefers), never by preference, because a 2-param leaf function has no hard $a2/$a3/$v1 anywhere for set_preference to key on. The tail const is local-allocated to $v0 as the first quantity born in the join block; target's $a0 needs both $v0 and $v1 occupied there, which local-alloc cannot see because lo and hi are global allocnos. LEVERS MEASURED THIS ROUND - inert at the 51-insn stream (no role register moved): tail-OR left-assoc, `pkt|hi` operand swap, pkt declared first, u32 pkt, lo computed before hi in the arms, s16/s32 named limit locals (one or both clamps), a separate sign-extended compare variable, and `tx = arg0` instead of `tx = x` (GCC CSEs it back to the carrier). Structural regressions: const folded into both arms (50 insns), separate join variable (50), s32 tx (49), early-declared const local (46 linediff). NOTABLE NEAR-MISS: an `s32 lim` named limit local DOES put the carrier in $a3 (the hardest role) but CSEs `lim-1` and loses the limit-save insn (50). src/display.c reverted; working tree clean apart from metrics/events.jsonl. Reusable tooling left in tmp/: c7a0_apply.py (body swap from a pristine backup), c7a0_batch.sh + c7a0_roles.py (~12 s per variant, prints the role->register map), c7a0_sbs.sh (side-by-side listing), c7a0_model.sh (extract + simulate), c7a0_what_if.py (model deltas -> allocation).

sessions.note: Round 17 tested the variable-reuse family (team-lead directed: make `hi` the SAME C variable as a real value already live before the x-clamp, per defeat-licm-hoist-var-reuse / staged-value-reused-variable) and then CLOSED the pure-C search space for the register assignment. EMPIRICAL: all five reuse spellings break the 51-insn stream - hi = x-limit save (50 insns), hi = y-limit save (49), hi = both limit saves (46), hi = sign-extended y (50), lo = x-limit save (50). Cause: naming a limit in a variable lets GCC CSE `limit - 1` and the limit-save instruction disappears, the same collapse round 16 saw with `s32 lim`. EXHAUSTIVE: tmp/c7a0_a2_scan.py enumerates all 273 single-atom perturbations of the model (refs, live length, preferences, conflict add/remove, hard-conflict removal across all 9 allocnos) and asks which put the x-clamp limit-save in $a2 - the atom that gates the whole cascade (83->a2 forces 94->a0, 92->a2, 81->a0, 76->a3). EXACTLY THREE atoms work and every one needs a hard register this function does not have: (1) `pref 76->r3`, the carrier copy-related to hard $v1 - no hard $v1 exists here, and it also lands hi in $a2 which is wrong; (2) `conf +78~83`, hi conflicting with the limit-save; (3) `pref 83->r6`, the limit-save copy-related to hard $a2, which is argument register 3 in a function that takes two. A 2-parameter leaf function has exactly three hard registers in scope ($a0, $a1, $v0) and set_preference only fires on a hard reg or a local-alloc pseudo already renumbered to one, so $a2/$a3/$v1 can never be PREFERRED - only reached by exclusion, whose sole source is a conflict with an allocno already holding $v1. ROUTE (2) IS DISPROVEN FROM THE BYTES, not from search: liveness starts at a def, so hi living across the x-clamp needs an instruction writing it there; tmp/c7a0_v1_census.py over target's own stream shows the first $v1 definition is insn 39 (`andi v1,a1,0xfff`) and the destination registers written before it are a0, a1, a2, a3, sp, v0 - no $v1 - while the limit-save's range is insn 9 to 13. So in target's OWN compilation hi and the limit-save cannot conflict, which means the round-16 model's 9/9 solution is not the mechanism the original used. CONSEQUENCE: within the pre-reload allocator the ra_solver simulates, target's allocation is unreachable from ANY stream-exact two-parameter leaf body. The only unmodeled path left is reload's spill-retry (the ra_solver README's known saTan4FireDisp divergence), but target's frame is `addiu sp,sp,-16` with vars=16 - no spill slots - so that looks closed too. RECOMMENDATION: stop spending rounds on C spellings for this allocation; the next legitimate moves are a mechanism outside the modeled allocator path or an owner disposition decision. Also relevant to the team-lead's `argument dataflow` hypothesis: it is CORRECT in substance (the values do need argument-register residency) but the function's own signature cannot supply it - the three call sites in src/display.c (lines 333, 396, 472) all pass exactly two arguments, and an unused third parameter generates no copy insn and therefore no preference. src reverted; oracle re-verified at 62efab4f73f992798c43e8c730aa43baa10bb4fa.
